Specifically, ARG represents relationships among sampled haplotypes across genome series local genealogies connected recombination events. genealogies describe haplotypes coalesce time can use estimate time recent common ancestor lineages (TMRCAB), well time recent common ancestor within lineage (TMRCAW). ARGs variety applications population genetics, including characterizing patterns ancestry genetic variation across genome. example, ARGs can used investigate distribution mutations genetic variants, signatures natural selection, patterns introgression populations species (Lewanski et al. 2024). retaining information local genealogies relationships across genome, ARGs can provide insights evolutionary processes may difficult distinguish using individual gene trees summary statistics alone.

title: Formatting data for ARGHelpR
text: script convert output ARG-Needle (Zhang et al., 2023). can combine ARGs chromosome use ARGHelpR (see cat command ).
code: import arg_needle_lib import tskit  def export_arg_to_tree_bed(argn_path, chromosome, output_bed):     # Load the inferred ARG from the .argn file     arg_obj = arg_needle_lib.load_arg(argn_path)          # Convert the ARG object to a tskit TreeSequence object     # This automatically splits the genome into non-recombining interval segments     ts = arg_needle_lib.arg_to_tskit(arg_obj)          # Write intervals in bed format     with open(output_bed, 'w') as bed_file:         # Iterate through each local tree segment along the sequence length         for tree in ts.trees():             # Get start and end positions for the interval             start = int(tree.interval.left)             end = int(tree.interval.right)                          # Generate the Newick string phylogeny             newick_str = tree.newick()                          # Write out bed file             bed_file.write(f"{chromosome}\t{start}\t{end}\t{newick_str}\n")  # Example Usage: export_arg_to_tree_bed("myarg.argn", "chr1", "myarg_chr1_trees.bed")

title: Formatting data for ARGHelpR
text: script convert output tsinfer (Kelleher et al., 2019). can combine ARGs chromosome use ARGHelpR (see cat command ). Please reach Keaka Farleigh questions.
code: import tskit  def ts_to_bed(tree_sequence_path, chromosome, output_bed):        # Load the ARG     ts = tskit.load(tree_sequence_path)          with open(output_bed, "w") as bed_file:         # Iterate through every local tree along the genome         for tree in ts.trees():             # Get start and end positions for the interval             start = int(tree.interval.left)             end = int(tree.interval.right)                          # Generate the Newick string phylogeny             newick_tree = tree.newick()                          # Write out bed file             bed_file.write(f"{chromosome}\t{start}\t{end}\t{newick_tree}\n")  # Example Usage: ts_to_bed("myarg.trees", "chr1", "myarg_chr1_trees.bed")

Users can also supply number cores use n.cores argument parallelize calculations. dataset small, whole genome data can large parallelization way make compute time reasonable. can also specify n.haps argument, influences ARGHelpR calculates time recent common ancestor within (TMRCAW) statistic. n.cores n.haps optional. Awesome, now data data frame. can use input identify_argcandidates_divergence identify_argcandidates_shared identify evidence selection /introgression.

title: arghelpr-vignette
text: use identify_argcandidates_divergence identify ARGs exhibitng patterns expect different forms selection, can read identifying selection introgression article understand test works. Briefly, use patterns time recent common ancestor (TMRCAB) time recent common ancestor within (TMRCAW) populations/species identify possible evidence selection. ARGHelpR can identify candidates without user-specified genomic background (background argument). background argument supplied thresholds set based , left empty ARGHelpR uses supplied distributions determine thresholds. Users can also specify thresholds using different threshold arguments. see ARGs associated divergence scenario, supporting different forms selection influencing different regions genome.
code: divergence_cands <- identify_argcandidates_divergence(dat = snake_argstats_df, analysis = "all")  # Bind together into a data frame   divergence_cands_df <- do.call("rbind", divergence_cands)  # Make a column telling us which scenario each ARG was identified as divergence_cands_df$scenario <- rownames(divergence_cands_df)  divergence_cands_df$scenario <- sub("\\..*", "", divergence_cands_df$scenario)  # How many of each scenario do we have? table(divergence_cands_df$scenario) #>  #>   RI RIWP   RS   WP  #>   51    1   32   37

TMRCAW also supposed reduced one populations scenario recurrent selection. can focus ARG tips, adjusting scale.  see TMRCAW also reduced relative background pop 2, thus confirming recurrent selection ARG matches expected patterns TMRCAB TMRCAW. Thank interest ARGHelpR, please contact Keaka Farleigh questions suggestions.
code: # Select an ARG to plot arg_toplot <- snake_argstats_df[8,19]  single_plot <- argplot(arg_toplot, pop1 = pop1$sample, pop2 = pop2$sample, col = c('#7D83FF', '#007FFF'), font.size = 0.75)  # We can change the scale to single_plot_scale <- argplot(arg_toplot, pop1 = pop1$sample, pop2 = pop2$sample, col = c('#7D83FF', '#007FFF'), scale = c(0,275000), font.size = 0.75) # Let's plot a couple of ARGs together par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5))  arg_toplot1 <- snake_argstats_df[8,19]  arg_toplot2 <- divergence_cands_df[91,19]  plot1 <- argplot(arg_toplot1, pop1 = pop1$sample, pop2 = pop2$sample, col = c('#7D83FF', '#007FFF'), scale = c(0,275000), font.size = 0.3)  rs_plot <- argplot(arg_toplot2, pop1 = pop1$sample, pop2 = pop2$sample, col = c('#7D83FF', '#007FFF'), scale = c(0,275000), font.size = 0.3) # Let's plot a couple of ARGs together par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5))  arg_toplot1 <- snake_argstats_df[8,19]  arg_toplot2 <- divergence_cands_df[91,19]  plot1_tips <- argplot(arg_toplot1, pop1 = pop1$sample, pop2 = pop2$sample, col = c('#7D83FF', '#007FFF'), scale = c(0,1000), font.size = 0.3)  rs_plot_tips <- argplot(arg_toplot2, pop1 = pop1$sample, pop2 = pop2$sample, col = c('#7D83FF', '#007FFF'), scale = c(0,1000), font.size = 0.3)
